newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ciller says Turk Telekom ruling aids all sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Ciller says Turk Telekom ruling aids all sell-offs.

text.p: Turkey's Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said the court approval of Turk Telekom's sale would pave the way for the rest of a privatisation programme expected by the government to raise over $5 billion this year.
"With this decision by the constitutional court the way is opened for the rest of privatisation," Ciller told reporters.
The constitutional court earlier rejected most of a challenge by 116 opposition MPs to the sell-off.
The Islamist-led government hopes to raise $3.5 billion from the telecommunications sale, which has been halted three times by the constitutional court since 1993.
Turkey's privatisation programme has moved sluggishly since its inception 10 years ago, raising total revenues of just $3 billion despite bold government forecasts each year.
The Istanbul stock market surged on the news, with the main index jumping 7.2 percent on the day in early afternoon trading.
Transport Minister Omer Barutcu told Reuters the sale of a maximum 10 percent of Telekom in the first tranche would be aimed at testing the market.
"Ten percent will be issued to assess our market condition at that time," he said, noting that under the privatisation 49 percent of Telekom is aimed to be sold.
A consortium headed by Goldman Sachs was last month appointed to advise on the sell-off.
